sources.title: Tribological performances of UHMWPE and PEEK under dry sliding conditions against steel and various polyetherimide polymer counterfaces
sources.access: Indexed publication abstract; direct publisher DOI and direct page access failed. Full methods unavailable.
sources.evidence: Abstract gives UHMWPE against GP-PEI60N,COF0.0728,SWR7.96e-15m2/N; transfer film attributed. Loads20/40/60N; speed constant but numeric speed not available in accessed text.
sources.limit: Exact resin grade, roughness, test temperature, speed, run-in path and dispersion not established. Pin wear is not PEI counterface wear; not50C ski evidence.

sources.title: SABIC ULTEM Resin1000 material data
sources.evidence: Typical density1270kg/m3; tensile modulus3200MPa; injection melt350-410C; amorphous unfilled PEI.
sources.limit: Catalog identity not proven same asS1 GP-PEI. Mechanical data not50C transient ski-contact or environmental safety qualification.

sources.title: Semi-analytical calculation model for friction of polymers on the example of POM|PE-UHMW and steel|PE-UHMW
sources.access: Publisher abstract and references read; full PDF not read
sources.evidence: Dry tests and silicone-oil separation tests; adhesion contribution and continuous/discontinuous motion matter.
sources.limit: Do not adopt silicone oil. Proportions not universal; no exact micron-grain50C coefficients imported.

sources.title: Sliding wear behaviour of oriented ultrahigh molecular weight polyethylene
sources.evidence: Tensile orientation reduced dry dissipated energy and wear under described study conditions; direction dependence.
sources.limit: No general crystallinity-to-glide rule or50C particle value.

sources.title: Wear and friction resistance of UHMWPE with anisotropic microstructure shaped by mechanical compression
sources.access: Indexed publisher abstract read; direct publisher returned403
sources.evidence: Compressed UHMWPE showed greater debris despite crystalline alignment under severe wear above elastic limit.
sources.limit: Different preparation and loading thanS4, not a same-condition replication; do not conclude every orientation process worsens wear.

sources.title: Tribological behavior of polyoxymethylene sliding against polyethylene and duplex steel in artificial seawater lubrication
sources.access: Indexed publisher abstract/highlights read; direct page error
sources.evidence: POM-PE lubricated pairing and transfer-film behavior
sources.limit: Artificial seawater is not dry summer or rainwater. No salt lubrication adopted, no coefficients used.
